rationale:
Split into two obligations that do not involve varifolds and that the supplied proof already isolates. The parent keeps only its limiting glue.

(1) cylinder_cutoff = steps 2–3. One C_c cut-off F on ℝ^N × G(N,n) satisfies ν(K_a) ≤ ofReal ∫F dν ≤ ν(K_b) for every measure ν that is finite on K_b. This is the most technical Lean part: bundling C_c over the compact Grassmannian, Borel product measurability, integrability by domination, and the Bochner-to-Lebesgue switch. It can be reused in any argument that reads ball masses off vague convergence.

(2) vague_cylinder_bounds = the fixed-ρ' parts of steps 4–5, which includes eventual finiteness for large j. It is a portmanteau-type inequality: for VagueConverges sequences whose cylinder masses converge, with finite outer limit, μ(K_a) ≤ Lb and La ≤ μ(K_b). It depends on (1).

Parent assembly from the children (steps 1, ρ'↓ρ and 6), checked in Lean:
- From IsVarifoldTangent obtain t_j > 0, t_j → 0 and VagueConverges (j ↦ rescaledMeasure V x (t j)) C.measure; then t → 𝓝[>]0.
- Compose the accepted sibling varifold_tangents_rescaled_ball_mass_tendsto (with θ := ofReal θ₀) with t. This gives V_j(K_r) → L(r) := ofReal θ₀ · ω_n · ofReal r^n, which is finite because ω_n < ∞.
- C.measure(K_r) < ∞ by C.finite_on_compact.
- For each ρ' > ρ, child 2 with (a, b, La, Lb) = (ρ, ρ', L ρ, L ρ') gives C.measure(K_ρ) ≤ L(ρ') and L(ρ) ≤ C.measure(K_ρ').
- L is continuous (ENNReal.continuous_const_mul ∘ pow ∘ ofReal). The map r ↦ C.measure(K_r) is right-continuous at ρ by tendsto_measure_biInter_gt, using ⋂_{r>ρ} K_r = K_ρ and C.measure(K_{ρ+1}) < ∞. So ge_of_tendsto along 𝓝[>]ρ gives both inequalities at ρ.
- Varifold.weight_apply turns C.weight(closedBall 0 ρ) into C.measure(K_ρ), and le_antisymm concludes.

subproblems.title: A C_c cut-off on ℝ^N × G(N,n) sandwiching closed-ball cylinder masses
subproblems.statement: Let N, n ∈ ℕ, G := Grassmannian N n (SimonGMT's projection-matrix Grassmannian), and for r ∈ ℝ let K_r := closedBall (0 : ℝ^N) r ×ˢ univ ⊆ ℝ^N × G. For all real a < b there is a single F ∈ C_c(ℝ^N × G, ℝ), chosen before the measure, such that every measure ν on ℝ^N × G with ν(K_b) ≠ ∞ satisfies ν(K_a) ≤ ofReal(∫ F dν) and ofReal(∫ F dν) ≤ ν(K_b). (∫ is the Bochner integral, which is 0 for non-integrable integrands, as in Lean.)
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (N n : ℕ) (a b : ℝ), a < b → ∃ F : C_c(Euclidean N × Grassmannian N n, ℝ), ∀ ν : Measure (Euclidean N × Grassmannian N n), ν (closedBall (0 : Euclidean N) b ×ˢ (univ : Set (Grassmannian N n))) ≠ ∞ → ν (closedBall (0 : Euclidean N) a ×ˢ (univ : Set (Grassmannian N n))) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (∫ z, F z ∂ν) ∧ ENNReal.ofReal (∫ z, F z ∂ν) ≤ ν (closedBall (0 : Euclidean N) b ×ˢ (univ : Set (Grassmannian N n)))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 2–3 of the parent proof (the cut-off functions behind Simon Ch. 8, 5.2), for arbitrary real a < b; the parent proof only needs 0 < a < b.

Notation:
- G := Grassmannian N n is a compact space (SimonGMT Grassmannian.instCompactSpace) and second countable (Grassmannian.instSecondCountableTopology). So the product σ-algebra on ℝ^N × G is the Borel σ-algebra of the product topology.
- K_r := closedBall (0 : ℝ^N) r ×ˢ univ.
- d := b − a > 0.

1. (The cut-off.) Define h : ℝ^N × G → ℝ by h(y, S) := min(1, max(0, (b − ‖y‖)/d)). It is continuous: (y, S) ↦ ‖y‖ is the norm composed with the continuous first projection; subtracting from the constant b and dividing by the nonzero constant d are continuous; and min/max with constants are continuous.
2. (Pointwise values.) For every z, 0 ≤ h z because max(0, ·) ≥ 0 and 1 ≥ 0, and h z ≤ 1 because of the min with 1.
   - If z = (y, S) ∈ K_a, i.e. ‖y‖ ≤ a, then b − ‖y‖ ≥ b − a = d, so (b − ‖y‖)/d ≥ 1 (as d > 0). Hence max(0, (b − ‖y‖)/d) = (b − ‖y‖)/d ≥ 1 and h z = 1.
   - If z = (y, S) ∉ K_b, i.e. ‖y‖ > b, then b − ‖y‖ < 0 and d > 0, so (b − ‖y‖)/d ≤ 0. Hence max(0, (b − ‖y‖)/d) = 0 and h z = min(1, 0) = 0.
3. (Compact support; definition of F.) closedBall 0 b is compact in the finite-dimensional normed space ℝ^N (a proper space), and univ is compact in the compact space G, so K_b is compact as a product of compact sets. By step 2, h z = 0 for every z ∉ K_b, so h has compact support (HasCompactSupport.intro: a function vanishing outside a compact subset of a Hausdorff space has compact support). Let F ∈ C_c(ℝ^N × G, ℝ) be the bundled compactly supported continuous map with underlying function h, so F z = h z for all z. F is chosen once and for all, independently of any measure.
4. (Measurability and integrability.) Now let ν be any measure on ℝ^N × G with ν(K_b) ≠ ∞.
   - K_a and K_b are measurable: closed balls are closed, hence Borel, and the product with univ is measurable.
   - F is continuous, hence (a.e.-)strongly measurable for the Borel product σ-algebra.
   - For every z, |F z| ≤ 1_{K_b}(z): if z ∈ K_b then |F z| = F z ≤ 1 by step 2; if z ∉ K_b then F z = 0 by step 2.
   - The indicator 1_{K_b} of the constant 1 is ν-integrable because K_b is measurable and ν(K_b) < ∞ (integrable_indicator_iff and integrableOn_const).
   - By domination (Integrable.mono'), F is ν-integrable.
5. (Bochner to Lebesgue.) Since F is ν-integrable and F ≥ 0 everywhere, ofReal(∫ F dν) = ∫⁻ ofReal(F z) dν(z) (ofReal_integral_eq_lintegral_ofReal).
6. (Lower bound.) For every z, 1_{K_a}(z) ≤ ofReal(F z): if z ∈ K_a, then F z = 1 by step 2 and ofReal 1 = 1; otherwise the left side is 0. Since K_a is measurable, ∫⁻ 1_{K_a} dν = ν(K_a) (lintegral_indicator_one). By monotonicity of the lower integral and step 5, ν(K_a) ≤ ∫⁻ ofReal(F) dν = ofReal(∫ F dν).
7. (Upper bound.) For every z, ofReal(F z) ≤ 1_{K_b}(z): if z ∈ K_b, then ofReal(F z) ≤ ofReal 1 = 1 since F z ≤ 1 and ofReal is monotone; if z ∉ K_b, then F z = 0 and ofReal 0 = 0. Since K_b is measurable, ∫⁻ 1_{K_b} dν = ν(K_b). By monotonicity and step 5, ofReal(∫ F dν) = ∫⁻ ofReal(F) dν ≤ ν(K_b).
8. (Conclusion.) The single F of step 3 satisfies ν(K_a) ≤ ofReal(∫ F dν) ≤ ν(K_b) for every measure ν with ν(K_b) ≠ ∞, which is the claim. No positivity of a or b is needed: for example, if a < 0 then K_a = ∅ and step 6 is trivially true, but steps 1–7 hold uniformly.
proof_key_steps: Define F(y,S) := min(1, max(0, (b − ‖y‖)/(b − a))). It is continuous, 0 ≤ F ≤ 1, F = 1 on K_a and F = 0 off K_b.
K_b = closedBall 0 b × G is compact (ℝ^N is proper, G is compact), so F vanishing off K_b makes it an element of C_c(ℝ^N × G, ℝ).
For ν(K_b) < ∞: |F| ≤ 1_{K_b} gives ν-integrability, and ofReal(∫F dν) = ∫⁻ ofReal(F) dν.
Pointwise 1_{K_a} ≤ ofReal ∘ F ≤ 1_{K_b} and monotonicity of the lower integral give ν(K_a) ≤ ofReal(∫F dν) ≤ ν(K_b).

subproblems.title: Vague limits versus closed-ball cylinder masses: μ(K_a) ≤ lim μ_j(K_b) and lim μ_j(K_a) ≤ μ(K_b) for a < b
subproblems.statement: Let N, n ∈ ℕ, G := Grassmannian N n and K_r := closedBall (0 : ℝ^N) r ×ˢ univ ⊆ ℝ^N × G. Let μs : ℕ → Measure(ℝ^N × G), and let μ be a measure on ℝ^N × G with VagueConverges μs μ: for every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^N × G, ℝ), ∫ f dμs_j → ∫ f dμ in ℝ as j → ∞. (∫ is the Bochner integral, which is 0 for non-integrable integrands, as in Lean.) Let a < b be real and La, Lb ∈ [0, ∞]. Assume μ(K_b) ≠ ∞, μs_j(K_a) → La and μs_j(K_b) → Lb in [0, ∞] as j → ∞, and Lb ≠ ∞. Then μ(K_a) ≤ Lb and La ≤ μ(K_b).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (N n : ℕ) (μs : ℕ → Measure (Euclidean N × Grassmannian N n)) (μ : Measure (Euclidean N × Grassmannian N n)) (a b : ℝ) (La Lb : ℝ≥0∞), VagueConverges μs μ → a < b → μ (closedBall (0 : Euclidean N) b ×ˢ (univ : Set (Grassmannian N n))) ≠ ∞ → Tendsto (fun j ↦ μs j (closedBall (0 : Euclidean N) a ×ˢ (univ : Set (Grassmannian N n)))) atTop (𝓝 La) → Tendsto (fun j ↦ μs j (closedBall (0 : Euclidean N) b ×ˢ (univ : Set (Grassmannian N n)))) atTop (𝓝 Lb) → Lb ≠ ∞ → μ (closedBall (0 : Euclidean N) a ×ˢ (univ : Set (Grassmannian N n))) ≤ Lb ∧ La ≤ μ (closedBall (0 : Euclidean N) b ×ˢ (univ : Set (Grassmannian N n)))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 4–5 of the parent proof for one fixed pair ρ < ρ' (here a < b), with the limiting masses abstracted to La and Lb.

Notation: G := Grassmannian N n and K_r := closedBall (0 : ℝ^N) r ×ˢ univ ⊆ ℝ^N × G. VagueConverges μs μ means ∫ f dμs_j → ∫ f dμ in ℝ for every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^N × G, ℝ).

1. (Cut-off.) Apply the sibling cylinder_cutoff (Lean: Submission.varifold_tangents_lbm_exists_cylinder_cutoff) to N, n, a, b and a < b. It gives F ∈ C_c(ℝ^N × G, ℝ) such that every measure ν on ℝ^N × G with ν(K_b) ≠ ∞ satisfies ν(K_a) ≤ ofReal(∫ F dν) and ofReal(∫ F dν) ≤ ν(K_b).
2. (The limit measure.) Apply step 1 to ν = μ, which is allowed since μ(K_b) ≠ ∞: μ(K_a) ≤ ofReal(∫ F dμ) ≤ μ(K_b).
3. (Eventual finiteness and comparison.) Since Lb < ∞, the set {c ∈ [0, ∞] : c < ∞} is an open neighbourhood of Lb (Iio ∞ ∈ 𝓝 Lb). So μs_j(K_b) → Lb implies μs_j(K_b) < ∞, i.e. μs_j(K_b) ≠ ∞, for all sufficiently large j. For each such j, step 1 with ν = μs_j gives μs_j(K_a) ≤ ofReal(∫ F dμs_j) ≤ μs_j(K_b). Thus both inequalities hold eventually along atTop.
4. (Convergence of the cut-off integrals.) VagueConverges μs μ applied to f = F gives ∫ F dμs_j → ∫ F dμ in ℝ. Since ENNReal.ofReal : ℝ → [0, ∞] is continuous, ofReal(∫ F dμs_j) → ofReal(∫ F dμ).
5. (Upper bound.) In the order-closed topology of [0, ∞], limits along the nontrivial filter atTop preserve eventual inequalities (le_of_tendsto_of_tendsto). Apply this to the eventual inequality ofReal(∫ F dμs_j) ≤ μs_j(K_b) of step 3, with limits ofReal(∫ F dμ) (step 4) and Lb (hypothesis). This gives ofReal(∫ F dμ) ≤ Lb. With step 2, μ(K_a) ≤ ofReal(∫ F dμ) ≤ Lb.
6. (Lower bound.) Apply the same principle to the eventual inequality μs_j(K_a) ≤ ofReal(∫ F dμs_j) of step 3, with limits La (hypothesis) and ofReal(∫ F dμ) (step 4). This gives La ≤ ofReal(∫ F dμ). With step 2, La ≤ ofReal(∫ F dμ) ≤ μ(K_b).
7. (Conclusion.) μ(K_a) ≤ Lb and La ≤ μ(K_b).
proof_key_steps: Take the cut-off F of cylinder_cutoff for a < b. Since μ(K_b) < ∞, it gives μ(K_a) ≤ ofReal(∫F dμ) ≤ μ(K_b).
Lb < ∞ forces μs_j(K_b) < ∞ eventually, so eventually μs_j(K_a) ≤ ofReal(∫F dμs_j) ≤ μs_j(K_b).
VagueConverges and continuity of ENNReal.ofReal give ofReal(∫F dμs_j) → ofReal(∫F dμ).
Limits preserve eventual inequalities: ofReal(∫F dμ) ≤ Lb and La ≤ ofReal(∫F dμ); combining with the first step gives μ(K_a) ≤ Lb and La ≤ μ(K_b).
